scope: Introductory orientation, not complete denominational histories. Entries marked research prospect identify work still to do. No current population figures, religious superiority rankings or private doctrines are inferred.

entries.name: Qumran texts and Essene comparisons
entries.description: The Dead Sea Scrolls contain multiple works and forms of community organization. Particular sectarian texts can be compared with reports about Essenes without making every manuscript the work of one monastic group.
entries.next: Compare individual Community Rule witnesses, War Scroll passages and external reports separately; retain disagreement about communities and dates.

entries.name: Sethian writings
entries.description: A scholarly grouping includes writings with distinctive divine genealogies and a lower ruler. A common classification does not establish one fixed institution or two independent primordial creators in every tractate.
entries.next: Develop an Apocryphon of John recension comparison with exact passage locators, rather than a generic definition of all Gnosticism.

entries.name: Valentinian traditions
entries.description: Ptolemy's intermediate just maker and Philip's ritual mysteries complicate the assumption that all esoteric Christians condemned the same evil creator and rejected all ritual.
entries.next: Distinguish named teachers, texts associated by scholars with the tradition, and testimony transmitted by opponents.

entries.name: Basilides and Basilidian testimony
entries.description: Irenaeus I.24 reports a system associated with Basilides, but it remains an opponent's account. It cannot serve as an unquestioned transcript of all Basilidian belief and conduct.
entries.next: Compare Irenaeus, Hippolytus and surviving fragments before building a complete doctrinal profile.

entries.name: Hermetic texts
entries.description: Hermetic works in Nag Hammadi Codex VI include a prayer joining knowledge, embodied transformation and a shared meal. Physical collection with other writings does not imply identical doctrine.
entries.next: Compare the Prayer of Thanksgiving's witnesses and the Discourse on the Eighth and Ninth in critical editions.

entries.name: Marcion and Marcionite traditions
entries.description: The tradition belongs in questions about scripture, law and the relation between creator and redeemer. It should not be equated automatically with every Sethian or Valentinian position.
entries.next: Add a dedicated primary-source dossier distinguishing hostile testimony, canon reconstruction and later Marcionite communities.

entries.name: Manichaeism
entries.description: The two principles, rescue of light and distinct community obligations need to be studied together. Invoking Jesus, Buddha and Zoroaster does not make their teachings interchangeable.
entries.next: Add named Syriac, Coptic, Iranian and Chinese witnesses, preserving which formulation belongs to which source.

entries.name: Zoroastrian traditions
entries.description: The relationships among Ahura Mazda and opposing spirits vary across historical texts and interpretations. One equal-two-gods formula is not an adequate description of every period.
entries.next: Compare defined Gathic, later Avestan and Middle Persian passages and add contemporary community perspectives.

entries.name: Buddhist traditions
entries.description: The nonself discourse supplies a precise comparison with a substantial liberated light-soul. Shared ascetic vocabulary does not establish an identical account of personhood.
entries.next: Expand beyond the selected early discourse without treating all Buddhist schools as one metaphysical system.

entries.name: Mandaeans
entries.description: A living tradition with distinctive scriptures, rites and community self-understanding. Its Book of John is not a canonical Christian Gospel, and Miriai's narrative requires its own textual treatment.
entries.next: Recover the critical Book of John and a clearly identified Ginza translation; compare actual sections rather than a composite end-times story.

entries.name: Rabbinic Judaism: Orthodox, Conservative and Reform
entries.description: These labels should receive separate institutional and historical entries. This edition does not infer a uniform attitude to Jesus or mysticism from a single medieval author or modern declaration.
entries.next: Obtain each movement's own statements and independent histories before presenting its current doctrine or membership as settled.

entries.name: Kabbalah and Hasidic traditions
entries.description: Tanya supplies one account of divine vitality, the other side and repentance. It is not evidence that all Jewish mystics share one cosmology or now accept Christian doctrines.
entries.next: Add distinct Zoharic, Lurianic and Hasidic witnesses, preserving the difference between schools, texts and living communities.

entries.name: Karaite Judaism
entries.description: Rejection of rabbinic Oral Law as binding does not entail the absence of commentary, legal interpretation or inherited practice. The community's own reading-room catalogue demonstrates those genres.
entries.next: Develop passages on scriptural interpretation and practice using named Karaite authors rather than the formula only literal text.

entries.name: Samaritans
entries.description: The Samaritan museum presents a distinctive five-book Torah and priestly heritage. The community is not adequately described merely as an unusual modern Jewish denomination.
entries.next: Expand its own account of Gerizim, textual witnesses and rites; distinguish traditional ancestry from independently documented chronology.

entries.name: Beta Israel
entries.description: ANU Museum's Orit exhibit documents a named sacred scroll, eight-book contents and custodial history. It supplies a concrete starting point rather than a story of an unchanging community completely isolated for a fixed millennium.
entries.next: Add Ethiopian-language texts, priestly perspectives and histories of community change and migration.

entries.name: Anusim, conversos and crypto-Jewish histories
entries.description: Forced conversion, covert observance and later descendants concern historical circumstances and diverse identities, not one uniformly constituted denomination. Present identity must not be assigned from ancestry alone.
entries.next: Develop geographically and chronologically specified cases using archives and community testimony; do not assume every family transmitted identical practices.

entries.name: Coptic Orthodox and Coptic Catholic churches
entries.description: Distinguish the Coptic Orthodox Church from the Coptic Catholic Church. The 1973 Orthodox-Catholic declaration affirms Trinity and real humanity and divinity, not an anti-incarnational Gnostic creed.
entries.next: Add church-specific histories and rites without substituting ancient Egyptian manuscript geography for doctrinal identity.

entries.name: Maronite Catholic Church
entries.description: An Eastern Catholic church with its own tradition; communion with Rome does not mean every Catholic uses the Latin rite. An Eastern liturgy is not evidence of Gnostic cosmology.
entries.next: Add primary liturgical and synodal sources, with a dedicated historical chronology.

entries.name: Greek Orthodox and Melkite Greek Catholic traditions
entries.description: Shared Byzantine liturgical heritage does not erase distinct ecclesial communion. Greek Orthodox and Melkite Catholic labels should not be used as interchangeable names for one institution.
entries.next: Create separate entries for rites, councils, jurisdiction and regional history rather than a geography-based scale of mysticism.

entries.name: Assyrian Church of the East and Chaldean Catholic Church
entries.description: These require distinct church entries despite related East Syriac heritage. Neither the name Assyrian nor a historical label such as Nestorian constitutes a claim that the church is Gnostic.
entries.next: Compare their own Christological and liturgical documents and histories of communion; avoid reusing outdated leadership data.

entries.name: Saint Thomas Christians
entries.description: Kerala's Thomas Christian heritage now spans distinct church affiliations. Apostolic origins should be identified as a tradition rather than treated as a securely witnessed arrival date for every later community.
entries.next: Give the Syriac traditions and later Catholic, Orthodox and other institutional histories their own sources.

entries.name: Old Calendarist and True Orthodox jurisdictions
entries.description: A separate history of particular calendar controversies and jurisdictions is needed. Calendar usage alone should not be used to infer a church's communion status, esotericism or entire doctrine.
entries.next: Recover original synodal statements and distinguish use of the Julian calendar from a specific jurisdiction identifying itself as Old Calendarist.

entries.name: Latter-day Saints
entries.description: The church's own introduction affirms additional scripture and a Godhead account distinct from Nicene consubstantiality. Those claims should be represented in their own terms rather than called a surviving ancient Gnostic sect.
entries.next: Add primary doctrinal and historical entries while distinguishing religious claims from independently established events.

entries.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
entries.description: The cited official account rejects the Trinity and describes Jesus as a created Son. Nontrinitarian belief alone does not establish identity with a Jewish, Islamic or ancient Gnostic doctrine.
entries.next: Expand the movement's own scripture, resurrection and community history without adopting its evaluation of other religions.

entries.name: Sunni and Shia traditions
entries.description: Shared commitments coexist with differing accounts of authority, law and interpretation. These broad labels contain internal schools and communities rather than two completely uniform sets of practice.
entries.next: Build separate histories of jurisprudence, theology and imamship using sources specific to each school.

entries.name: Sufi traditions and orders
entries.description: Sufism describes devotional and interpretive streams and orders, not a mutually exclusive third denomination beside Sunni and Shia. Remembrance is one important practice, not the full identity of every order.
entries.next: Compare named teachers, texts and institutions; keep practice, doctrine and communal affiliation separate.

entries.name: Ahmadiyya Muslim traditions
entries.description: The community traces its foundation to Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in Qadian in 1889, in British India. Its prophetic and messianic claims and its Muslim self-identification need to be distinguished from other authorities' assessments.
entries.next: Add internal branches and disagreements through their own documents, rather than treating Ahmadiyya as a type of Sufi order.

entries.name: Ibadism
entries.description: Wilkinson's study describes a distinctive early school and the importance of Basran, Omani and North African histories. The chapter abstracts do not support treating every period as uniformly peaceful, democratic or unchanged.
entries.next: Read the complete study and primary community texts before expanding doctrinal and legal claims.

entries.name: Zaydi Shia traditions
entries.description: The movement associated with Zayd has distinctive accounts of imamship and a complex history. Describing it merely as the Shia group closest to Sunni Islam substitutes a single scale for that history.
entries.next: Compare specific doctrines of authority and law across time rather than universalizing a modern shorthand.

entries.name: Ismaili traditions
entries.description: The cited institutional account emphasizes interpretation and imamship from a Nizari setting. Its perspective is not automatically a description of all Ismaili branches, and esoteric interpretation is not proof of one Gnostic ancestry.
entries.next: Add separate Nizari and other Ismaili histories, primary texts and community accounts without moral rankings such as most progressive.

entries.name: Nation of Islam
entries.description: A named community source identifies its connection with Elijah Muhammad's teaching. A complete account must distinguish the movement's own claims, later organizational histories and other African American Muslim communities.
entries.next: Recover primary foundational texts and independently researched histories before generalizing from one study group.

entries.name: Druze tradition
entries.description: The Institute of Ismaili Studies lecture description locates formative developments in an eleventh-century Fatimid setting while examining a distinctive tradition. It does not authenticate the supplied list of secret sages.
entries.next: Add accessible primary and community sources with clearly bounded claims; do not invent closed teachings or equate all esotericism with one religion.

entries.name: Alawite / Nusayri traditions
entries.description: Friedman's study supplies a scholarly point of entry. Only publication and chapter metadata were available here; this record is not a completed account of restricted doctrines or every adherent's identity.
entries.next: Consult the full historical study and appropriate living-community sources, distinguishing Alawites from similarly named Alevi traditions.

entries.name: Yazidi tradition
entries.description: Oral sacred transmission and the disputed status of commonly circulated printed holy books require particular care. Hostile outsider labels are not reliable descriptions of the community's worship.
entries.next: Develop qawl and community-preservation entries using identified performers, versions and scholarly documentation.

entries.name: Baha'i Faith
entries.description: The community names Buddha and Zoroaster within progressive revelation, alongside other divine educators. This is its theology of religious relationship, not evidence that all earlier figures taught one identical system.
entries.next: Develop the meaning of Manifestation and the tradition's historical emergence through primary and independent sources.

entries.name: Rastafari
entries.description: The museum and scholarly records connect Jamaican origins, scriptural reinterpretation and religious symbolism. Interpretations of Selassie and community practice require attention to diversity rather than one imposed creed.
entries.next: Add named community voices and histories of houses, texts and practices, distinguishing religious claims from an external description.
